# React Spectrum / React Aria

> Accessibility- and i18n-focused React: React Aria for custom-branded systems, React Spectrum S2 for Adobe-style tools.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **90/100** |
| Maintainer | Adobe (org-backed) |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | headless (headless) |
| Install | CLI copies component source into your repo (requires: bundler) |
| Good for | enterprise, accessibility-critical, creative-tools, custom-brand |
| Dark mode / RTL | yes / yes |
| Package size (unpacked) | 6.8k KB |
| License | Apache-2.0 |
| Last activity | 2026-11-05 |
| Docs | https://react-spectrum.adobe.com |
| Source | https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum |

## Public usage & feedback
Numbers as reported by each source on 2026-11-05; nothing is estimated.

| Signal | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub stars | 16.0k | GitHub API (adobe/react-spectrum) |
| GitHub forks | 1.6k | GitHub API |
| Contributors (incl. anonymous) | 551 | GitHub API |

| npm weekly downloads | 8.5M | npm (`react-aria-components` 1.22.1) |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/llms.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@react-aria/mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"react-spectrum":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@react-aria/mcp"]}}}
    ```
- **Copy-the-source CLI:** documented at https://react-aria.adobe.com/getting-started.md
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/HEAD/packages/@react-spectrum/s2/style/tokens.ts
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you want a finished visual style out of the box. This is headless; you supply all styling.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v1, checked against https://react-aria.adobe.com/getting-started.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 1.22.1._

## Install
```bash
npm install react-aria-components     # React Aria: unstyled, accessible; bring your own styles
npm install @react-spectrum/s2        # React Spectrum S2: Adobe's styled components
```

## Setup
- **React Aria Components:** no provider. Start from the official vanilla-CSS or Tailwind examples (copy, download as ZIP, or install with the shadcn CLI from each example), or download a Storybook starter kit.
- **React Spectrum S2:** styling uses build-time style macros, so follow the bundler setup for your tool (Parcel, Vite, webpack, Next.js, React Router, Rollup, ESBuild) in the S2 getting-started guide.

## When to choose which
- **React Aria:** a custom brand that needs best-in-class accessibility and internationalisation (date pickers, comboboxes, drag and drop, tables).
- **React Spectrum S2:** Adobe-style creative and pro tools.

## Agent tips
- MCP servers: `npx @react-aria/mcp@latest` (React Aria) and `npx @react-spectrum/mcp@latest` (S2).
- Agent skills: `npx skills add https://react-aria.adobe.com` or `npx skills add https://react-spectrum.adobe.com`.
- LLM docs: `https://react-aria.adobe.com/llms.txt` and `https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/llms.txt` (every page has a `.md` version).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

  - `npx shadcn@latest mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"shadcn-ui":{"command":"npx","args":["shadcn@latest","mcp"]}}}
    ```
- **Copy-the-source CLI:** documented at https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli.md
- **Theming tokens:** Theme is CSS variables (globals.css) generated per registry theme; see ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v4, checked against https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 4.23.0._

## Install
New project (scaffolds the app and shadcn/ui together):
```bash
npx shadcn@latest init --template next     # templates: next, vite, start, react-router, laravel, astro
```
Existing project: run `npx shadcn@latest init` in the app root. Choose the primitive base with `--base radix|base|aria`, or a saved design with `--preset <code>` (build one at ui.shadcn.com/create). Then add components:
```bash
npx shadcn@latest add button card dialog field input table sidebar
```

## How it works
Components are copied into your repo (`components/ui/*`), so you own and edit the source. Config lives in `components.json`. Built on Radix, Base UI or React Aria primitives with Tailwind CSS.

## Theme it to a brand
- Edit the CSS variables in your global CSS (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--radius`, …) for `:root` and `.dark`, or start from a preset.
- `npx shadcn@latest preset decode <code>` shows what a preset sets; `shadcn apply` re-applies one to an existing project.
- Fonts: set them in your layout and map them to `--font-sans`.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx shadcn@latest mcp init --client <claude|cursor|vscode|codex|opencode>`. It lets the agent search and install registry items.
- Agent skill: `npx skills add shadcn/ui`.
- `npx shadcn@latest docs <component>` and `view` print docs and source; `search` queries registries.
- Never hand-write a component that exists in the registry; `add` it. Use blocks (for example `npx shadcn@latest add dashboard-01`) to scaffold whole screens.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v9, checked against https://mantine.dev/llms/getting-started.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 9.7.5._

## Install
Quickest: start from an official template (Next.js or Vite) on mantine.dev. Existing app:
```bash
npm install @mantine/core @mantine/hooks
npm install --save-dev postcss postcss-preset-mantine postcss-simple-vars
# extras as needed: @mantine/form @mantine/dates dayjs @mantine/notifications @mantine/charts recharts
```
Create `postcss.config.cjs` with the `postcss-preset-mantine` and `postcss-simple-vars` plugins (breakpoint variables are listed in the getting-started guide).

## Setup
```tsx
import '@mantine/core/styles.css';   // once, at the root; other packages have their own styles.css
import { MantineProvider, createTheme } from '@mantine/core';
const theme = createTheme({ primaryColor: 'indigo', fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif', defaultRadius: 'md' });
export function App() { return <MantineProvider theme={theme} defaultColorScheme="auto">{/* app */}</MantineProvider>; }
```
With SSR (Next.js etc.): put `<ColorSchemeScript />` in `<head>` and spread `mantineHtmlProps` on `<html>` to avoid hydration warnings.

## Theme it to a brand
Everything goes through `createTheme`: `colors` (10-shade tuples), `primaryColor`, `fontFamily`, `headings`, `radius`, `spacing`, and per-component `components` defaults. Style custom parts with CSS modules and Mantine's CSS variables.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @mantine/mcp-server`. Docs index for LLMs: `https://mantine.dev/llms.txt` (every page has a Markdown twin under `/llms/`).
- Prefer Mantine's own `AppShell`, `useForm`, `notifications` and `@mantine/dates` over third-party libraries to keep one visual language.
- Create React App is not supported for new projects; use Vite or Next.js.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npx assistant-ui@latest create     # new app (templates: see the CLI reference)
npx assistant-ui@latest init       # add to an existing project
```
Add your model provider's API key to `.env` and run `npm run dev`. Components can also come from the shadcn CLI through the `@assistant-ui` registry in `components.json`.

## What you get
Composable primitives (Thread, Composer, Message, ActionBar) with runtimes for the AI SDK, LangGraph and custom backends; streaming, attachments and tool-call UIs.

## Agent tips
- Hosted MCP server (docs and examples, nothing to install): `https://www.assistant-ui.com/mcp` (streamable HTTP).
- Agent skills: `npx skills add assistant-ui/skills`. LLM docs: `https://www.assistant-ui.com/llms.txt`.
- Styling follows shadcn/ui, so use it with a shadcn base for the rest of the app.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

  - npm package `@chakra-ui/react-mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"chakra-ui":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@chakra-ui/react-mcp"]}}}
    ```
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/tree/HEAD/apps/mcp (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/HEAD/apps/www/public/r/theme/tokens
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/HEAD/CLAUDE.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use. Check the docs for RSC support.

_Hand-written guide for v3, checked against https://chakra-ui.com/llms-full.txt on 2026-11-05; latest release 3.38.0._

## Install
Requires Node.js 20+. Framework guides exist for Next.js and Vite.
```bash
npm i @chakra-ui/react @emotion/react
npx @chakra-ui/cli snippet add      # adds the Provider, color-mode and other snippets to your repo
```

## Setup
Wrap the app with the generated provider (it composes `ChakraProvider` and `next-themes` for colour mode):
```tsx
import { Provider } from '@/components/ui/provider';
export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return <html suppressHydrationWarning><body><Provider>{children}</Provider></body></html>;
}
```

## Theme it to a brand
```ts
import { createSystem, defaultConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
export const system = createSystem(defaultConfig, {
  theme: { tokens: { fonts: { heading: { value: "'Figtree', sans-serif" }, body: { value: "'Figtree', sans-serif" } } } },
});
```
Pass it to `ChakraProvider value={system}` inside the provider, and run `npx @chakra-ui/cli typegen src/theme.ts` for typed tokens. Token values are always wrapped in `{ value: … }`.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @chakra-ui/react-mcp`.
- LLM docs: `https://chakra-ui.com/llms.txt` links to focused files (components, styling, theming, v3 migration). v3 differs from v2; don't use v2 examples.
- Chakra still uses Emotion at runtime today; check the docs before relying on zero-runtime styling.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)

  - npm package `@heroui/react-mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"heroui":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@heroui/react-mcp"]}}}
    ```
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/heroui-inc/heroui/tree/HEAD/apps/docs (see its README for setup)

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v3, checked against https://heroui.com/docs/react/getting-started/quick-start.mdx on 2026-11-05; latest release 3.2.7._

## Install
Requires React 19+ and Tailwind CSS v4 (set Tailwind up first with its framework guide).
```bash
npm i @heroui/styles @heroui/react
```
In your main Tailwind CSS file, import HeroUI right after Tailwind (order matters):
```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@heroui/styles";
```

## Setup
No provider is needed in v3. Import components and use them:
```tsx
import { Button } from '@heroui/react';
export function App() { return <Button>My Button</Button>; }
```
Built on React Aria Components; components are composed from parts (for example `Card.Header`).

## Theme it to a brand
Themes are CSS variables on top of Tailwind v4's `@theme`. Set `class="light" data-theme="light"` (or `dark`) on `<html>`, and override semantic variables such as `--accent` and `--success` in `:root`, or under your own `[data-theme="brand"]` selector.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @heroui/react-mcp@latest`. HeroUI's own docs tell agents to treat the MCP as the source of truth for install steps and versions.
- v3 is a rewrite: v2 APIs (`HeroUIProvider`, the `heroui()` Tailwind plugin) no longer apply. The migration guide for agents is `https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/migration/agent-index`.
- Docs index: `https://www.heroui.com/llms.txt`; pages have `.mdx` source versions.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use. Check the docs for RSC support.

_Hand-written guide for v6, checked against https://ant.design/docs/react/getting-started.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 6.7.0._

## Install
```bash
npm install antd @ant-design/icons
# Next.js App Router: npm install @ant-design/nextjs-registry
```
antd 6 needs React 18 or newer and `@ant-design/icons` 6 (icons 6 does not work with antd 5).

## Setup
```tsx
import { ConfigProvider, App as AntApp, theme } from 'antd';
<ConfigProvider theme={{
  token: { colorPrimary: '#1677ff', borderRadius: 8, fontFamily: 'Inter' },
  algorithm: theme.defaultAlgorithm, // or theme.darkAlgorithm, theme.compactAlgorithm, or an array of them
}}>
  <AntApp>{/* app */}</AntApp>
</ConfigProvider>
```
Next.js App Router: wrap `{children}` in `app/layout.tsx` with `<AntdRegistry>` from `@ant-design/nextjs-registry`.

## Theme it to a brand
Global design tokens in `token`, per-component tokens in `components: { Button: { … } }`. Use `compactAlgorithm` for dense back-office screens.

## Agent tips
- antd 6 changed and deprecated many props (for example `Alert` `message` → `title`, `closeText` → `closable`). Don't trust v5 examples from memory.
- MCP server via the official CLI: `npx -y @ant-design/cli mcp`. The CLI also works offline: `antd info Button`, `antd doc Button`, `antd token DatePicker`.
- Agent skill: `npx skills add ant-design/ant-design-cli`. Docs for agents: `https://ant.design/docs/react/for-agents.md` and `https://ant.design/llms.txt`.
- For admin apps use ProComponents (`@ant-design/pro-components`): ProTable, ProForm and ProLayout save a lot of code.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npm install @carbon/react
npm install sass
```

## Setup
```scss
// index.scss: all component styles (or @use '@carbon/react/scss/components/button' for one)
@use '@carbon/react';
```
```tsx
import { Theme, Button } from '@carbon/react';
import { Add } from '@carbon/react/icons';

<Theme theme="white">{/* 'white' | 'g10' | 'g90' | 'g100' */}
  <Button renderIcon={Add}>Create</Button>
</Theme>
```
`Theme` can wrap the whole app or a single region (for example a dark `g100` header on a `white` page).

## Theme it to a brand
Carbon is intentionally opinionated: pick one of the four themes and customise through its Sass theme tokens rather than ad-hoc CSS.

## Agent tips
- Carbon MCP (hosted): `https://mcp.carbondesignsystem.com/mcp` (streamable HTTP). It requires signing in with an IBMid. A "Carbon Builder" agent skill is published in the carbon-mcp repository.
- Docs index for LLMs: `https://carbondesignsystem.com/llms.txt`.
- Use the UI Shell components (`Header`, `SideNav`) for app chrome and `DataTable` for tables. Web Components version: `@carbon/web-components`.

5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://mui.com/material-ui/llms.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@mui/mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"mui":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@mui/mcp"]}}}
    ```
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use. Check the docs for RSC support.

_Hand-written guide for v9, checked against https://mui.com/material-ui/getting-started/installation.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 9.5.0._

## Install
```bash
npm install @mui/material @emotion/react @emotion/styled
# optional: npm install @mui/icons-material @mui/x-data-grid @mui/x-date-pickers @mui/x-charts
```
React 18 or older: also pin `react-is` to your React version (for example `npm install react-is@18.3.1` plus an `overrides` entry in package.json), because Material UI uses `react-is@19`.

## Setup
```tsx
import { ThemeProvider, createTheme, CssBaseline } from '@mui/material';
const theme = createTheme({
  cssVariables: { colorSchemeSelector: 'class' },
  colorSchemes: { light: true, dark: true },
  palette: { primary: { main: '#4F46E5' } },
  shape: { borderRadius: 10 },
  typography: { fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif' },
});
export default function App() { return <ThemeProvider theme={theme}><CssBaseline />{/* app */}</ThemeProvider>; }
```
Next.js App Router: `npm install @mui/material-nextjs @emotion/cache`, then wrap `{children}` in `app/layout.tsx` with `AppRouterCacheProvider` from `@mui/material-nextjs/v15-appRouter` (use the `v1X-appRouter` path that matches your Next.js major).

## Theme it to a brand
All brand decisions go in `createTheme` (palette, typography, shape, `components` overrides). Avoid colour literals in `sx`; use `theme.palette.*` or the generated CSS variables (`var(--mui-palette-primary-main)`).

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @mui/mcp@latest`. It gives exact, versioned docs and code samples; prefer it over memory.
- Every docs page has a Markdown twin (append `.md`); the index is `https://mui.com/material-ui/llms.txt`.
- For data-heavy UI use MUI X (Data Grid, Date Pickers, Charts) instead of building tables and pickers by hand.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
Material widgets ship with the Flutter SDK: `flutter create my_app`.

## Setup
```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.indigo)),
  darkTheme: ThemeData(colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.indigo, brightness: Brightness.dark)),
  home: const HomePage(),
);
```
Material 3 is the default in current Flutter, so no flag is needed.

## Theme it to a brand
One seed colour generates the full Material 3 scheme; customise `textTheme` and component themes in `ThemeData`. Use `Cupertino*` widgets or `.adaptive` constructors where iOS fidelity matters.

## Agent tips
- Dart and Flutter MCP server (ships with the Dart SDK): `{"mcpServers": {"dart": {"command": "dart", "args": ["mcp-server"]}}}`. It lets agents analyse, run and hot-reload the app.
- Official agent skills: `npx skills add flutter/agent-plugins --skill '*'` and `npx skills add dart-lang/skills --skill '*'`.
- Docs index: `https://docs.flutter.dev/llms.txt`.

  - remote server https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"nuxt-ui":{"type":"http","url":"https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp"}}}
    ```

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v4, checked against https://ui.nuxt.com/raw/docs/getting-started/installation/nuxt.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 4.12.0._

## Install
New project from a template:
```bash
npm create nuxt@latest -- -t ui          # also: ui/landing, ui/docs, ui/saas, ui/dashboard, ui/chat
```
Existing Nuxt app:
```bash
npm install @nuxt/ui tailwindcss
```
Add `modules: ['@nuxt/ui']` and `css: ['~/assets/css/main.css']` to `nuxt.config.ts`, and in `app/assets/css/main.css`:
```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@nuxt/ui";
```
Plain Vue (Vite): same packages, then add the `ui()` plugin from `@nuxt/ui/vite` to `vite.config.ts`.

## Setup
Wrap the app in `<UApp>` (provides toasts, tooltips and overlays):
```vue
<template>
  <UApp>
    <NuxtPage />
  </UApp>
</template>
```

## Theme it to a brand
`app/app.config.ts`:
```ts
export default defineAppConfig({ ui: { colors: { primary: 'indigo', secondary: 'purple', neutral: 'zinc' } } })
```
Custom colour scales go in CSS with Tailwind's `@theme`; per-component `ui` props override slot classes.

## Agent tips
- Remote MCP server: `https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp` (HTTP transport). Docs index: `https://ui.nuxt.com/llms.txt`; every page has a raw Markdown version under `/raw/docs/…`.
- Start from the template closest to the product (dashboard, SaaS, chat, docs) rather than from scratch.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

  - **Access:** The official MCP server (Blueprint) is a paid subscription with a free trial [https://daisyui.com/blueprint/].

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v5, checked against https://daisyui.com/llms.txt on 2026-11-05; latest release 5.7.50._

## Install
daisyUI 5 requires Tailwind CSS 4 (no `tailwind.config.js`).
```bash
npm i -D daisyui@latest
```
```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@plugin "daisyui";
```
No build step (prototypes): the precompiled CSS plus the Tailwind browser build:
```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/daisyui@5" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" />
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tailwindcss/browser@4"></script>
```

## How it works
Semantic class names (`btn btn-primary`, `card`, `modal`) on plain HTML; works with any framework or none.

## Theme it to a brand
Pick built-in themes with `@plugin "daisyui" { themes: light --default, dark --prefersdark; }`, or define one:
```css
@plugin "daisyui/theme" {
  name: "brand";
  default: true;
  --color-primary: oklch(55% 0.2 260);
  --radius-box: 0.5rem;
}
```
The theme generator on daisyui.com produces these blocks.

## Agent tips
- `https://daisyui.com/llms.txt` is a compact, complete class reference; load it before writing markup. A free agent skill is offered on the install page.
- daisyUI's official MCP server (Blueprint) is a paid subscription with a free trial.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

| Frameworks | react, react-native |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://tamagui.dev/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://tamagui.dev/llms-full.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui/blob/HEAD/code/core/themes/src/tokens.ts
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use. Check the docs for RSC support.

_Hand-written guide for v3, checked against https://tamagui.dev/llms.txt on 2026-11-05; latest release 3.2.2._

## Install
New cross-platform app (Expo + Next.js starter):
```bash
npm create tamagui@latest
```
Existing app:
```bash
npm install tamagui @tamagui/config
```

## Setup
```tsx
// tamagui.config.ts
import { defaultConfig } from '@tamagui/config/v6';
import { createTamagui } from 'tamagui';
export const config = createTamagui(defaultConfig);
```
```tsx
import { TamaguiProvider } from 'tamagui';
import { config } from './tamagui.config';
<TamaguiProvider config={config} defaultTheme="light">{/* app */}</TamaguiProvider>
```
Import `tamagui.config.ts` in one place near the root.

## Theme it to a brand
Tokens and themes are typed in the config: use `$tokens` (`bg="$background"`, `p="$4"`), never raw values. `@tamagui/config/v6` provides sensible settings, themes and fonts; override parts of it rather than starting from zero.

## Agent tips
- Add the optimising compiler for production web builds: `npm i -D @tamagui/cli` and `tamaguiPlugin()` from `@tamagui/cli/vite` (equivalents exist for Next.js and Metro).
- Animations are pluggable drivers (CSS, Reanimated, Motion) configured in `createTamagui`.
- The full docs are a single LLM file at `https://tamagui.dev/llms.txt` (very large; search it rather than reading it whole).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Score breakdown
| Capability | Points |
|---|---|
| Official MCP server (agent can query components/docs live) | 0/20 |
| llms.txt on the docs site | 15/15 |
| llms-full.txt (whole docs as one markdown file) | 5/5 |
| Machine-readable design tokens in the repo | 15/15 |
| Typed component API (TypeScript / Swift / Kotlin / Dart / C#) | 10/10 |
| Registry / CLI install of component source (e.g. shadcn registry) | 10/10 |
| Agent docs: skills shipped in the package, or AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / cursor rules in the repo | 5/5 |
| Storybook / live, inspectable examples | 0/5 |
| Figma Code Connect (design ↔ code mapping) | 0/5 |
| Accessibility guidance shipped with the source | 5/5 |
| Dedicated documentation site | 5/5 |

Quality gate: activity **active**; traction via stars, npm.

_Hand-written guide for v5, checked against https://github.com/primefaces/primevue/tree/master/apps/showcase/doc/vite on 2026-11-05; latest release 5.0.4._

## Install
```bash
npm install primevue @primeuix/themes
```

## Setup
```ts
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import PrimeVue from 'primevue/config';
import Aura from '@primeuix/themes/aura';

const app = createApp(App);
app.use(PrimeVue, { theme: { preset: Aura, options: { darkModeSelector: '.dark' } } });
```
Nuxt: use the `@primevue/nuxt-module` module. Components can be auto-imported (see "Auto Import" in the docs).

## Theme it to a brand
`definePreset(Aura, { semantic: { primary: { 50: '{indigo.50}', …, 950: '{indigo.950}' } } })` from `@primeuix/themes`. Tailwind users can run PrimeVue in unstyled mode with pass-through classes.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @primevue/mcp`. Docs moved to primevue.dev; the LLM index is `https://primevue.dev/llms/llms.txt` (plus `llms-full.txt`).
- PrimeNG (Angular) and PrimeReact share the same theming model; PrimeNG's MCP is `@primeng/mcp`.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

  - remote server https://mcp.vuetifyjs.com/mcp
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"vuetify":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.vuetifyjs.com/mcp"}}}
    ```

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v4, checked against https://github.com/vuetifyjs/vuetify/blob/master/packages/docs/src/pages/en/getting-started/installation.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 4.3.2._

## Install
New project:
```bash
npm create vuetify@latest
```
Existing Vite app:
```bash
npm i vuetify
npm i -D vite-plugin-vuetify      # optional: tree-shaking and SASS variable support
npm i @mdi/font @fontsource/roboto
```
Nuxt: `npm i -D vuetify vite-plugin-vuetify` and register the plugin in `nuxt.config.ts` (see the installation guide).

## Setup
```ts
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import 'vuetify/styles';
import { createVuetify } from 'vuetify';
import * as components from 'vuetify/components';
import * as directives from 'vuetify/directives';
import '@mdi/font/css/materialdesignicons.css';
import '@fontsource/roboto';

const vuetify = createVuetify({ components, directives, theme: { defaultTheme: 'system' } });
createApp(App).use(vuetify).mount('#app');
```
Vuetify does not bundle the Roboto font; add it yourself (as above).

## Theme it to a brand
`createVuetify({ theme: { defaultTheme: 'light', themes: { light: { colors: { primary: '#4F46E5' } } } } })`. `defaultTheme` accepts `'system'` to follow the OS; switch at runtime with the theme instance's `change`, `toggle` or `cycle`.

## Agent tips
- Vuetify MCP (remote): `https://mcp.vuetifyjs.com/mcp`. It includes upgrade tools for moving from Vuetify 3 to 4.
- Vuetify 4 changed style entry points (`vuetify/styles/core`), typography, elevation and several component defaults; don't copy v3 examples blindly.
- Use `v-data-table` (or `v-data-table-server` for large data) instead of hand-built tables.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

_Hand-written guide for v5, checked against https://taiga-ui.dev/getting-started.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 5.31.0._

## Install
The schematic installs packages and configures styles, assets and providers:
```bash
ng add taiga-ui            # Angular CLI
# Nx: npm i taiga-ui && nx g taiga-ui:ng-add
```
Manual: `npm i @taiga-ui/{cdk,core,kit,icons}` plus add-ons as needed (`@taiga-ui/addon-charts`, `addon-table`, `addon-commerce`, `addon-mobile`, `layout`).

## Setup
```ts
// main.ts
import { provideTaiga } from '@taiga-ui/core';
bootstrapApplication(App, { providers: [provideTaiga()] });
```
```ts
// app component
import { TuiRoot } from '@taiga-ui/core';
@Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [TuiRoot], template: `<tui-root><!-- app --></tui-root>` })
export class App {}
```
Manual installs also add `@taiga-ui/styles/taiga-ui-theme.less` and `taiga-ui-fonts.less` to the build `styles`, and copy `@taiga-ui/icons/src` to `assets/taiga-ui/icons`.

## Theme it to a brand
Override Taiga's CSS variables (`--tui-background-accent-1`, `--tui-text-primary`, …) in a global stylesheet.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx @taiga-ui/mcp init` scaffolds the config for your agent (`--client <client>` to choose one). Docs index: `https://taiga-ui.dev/llms.txt`.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.


## Agent tips
- Read https://rsuitejs.com/llms.txt first. It indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Consider an alternative if
- you are not building inside the microsoft ecosystem.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use. Check the docs for RSC support.

_Hand-written guide for v9, checked against https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react//llms/concepts-developer-quick-start.txt on 2026-11-05; latest release 9.75.1._

## Install
```bash
npm install @fluentui/react-components
```

## Setup
```tsx
import { FluentProvider, webLightTheme } from '@fluentui/react-components';
<FluentProvider theme={webLightTheme}>{/* app */}</FluentProvider>
```
Fluent v9 styles with CSS-in-JS, so `FluentProvider` must sit at the root. Built-in themes include `webLightTheme`, `webDarkTheme`, `teamsLightTheme` and `teamsDarkTheme`.

## Theme it to a brand
Build a 16-step `BrandVariants` ramp (the Theme Designer in the docs generates one) and call `createLightTheme(brand)` / `createDarkTheme(brand)`. Style custom parts with `makeStyles` and `tokens`.

## Agent tips
- Use v9 (`@fluentui/react-components`), not v8 (`@fluentui/react`); they are different libraries.
- LLM docs: `https://react.fluentui.dev/llms.txt` (links to plain-text pages per topic).
- Known React strict-mode issues in development are tracked on GitHub; they don't affect production builds.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npm install react-native-paper react-native-safe-area-context
npm install @react-native-vector-icons/material-design-icons
npx pod-install      # iOS, bare React Native only
```
Optional, smaller production bundles: add `react-native-paper/babel` to the production `plugins` in your Babel config.

## Setup
```tsx
import { PaperProvider, MD3LightTheme } from 'react-native-paper';
const theme = { ...MD3LightTheme, colors: { ...MD3LightTheme.colors, primary: '#4F46E5' } };
<PaperProvider theme={theme}>{/* app */}</PaperProvider>
```

## Theme it to a brand
Generate a full Material 3 colour scheme from one brand colour (the theming guide links a generator) and paste it into `colors`; use `MD3DarkTheme` as the base for dark mode.

## Agent tips
- Pair with React Navigation; the docs cover theming navigation together with Paper.
- LLM index: `https://callstack.github.io/react-native-paper/llms.txt`; every page has a `.md` version.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.

5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@primer/mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"primer":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@primer/mcp"]}}}
    ```
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/primer/react/tree/HEAD/packages/mcp (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/primer/react/blob/HEAD/packages/react/src/Token/index.ts
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/primer/react/blob/HEAD/.github/copilot-instructions.md
- **Figma Code Connect:** yes, so Figma components map to code.

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v38, checked against https://primer.style/product/getting-started/react on 2026-11-05; latest release 38.44.0._

## Install
```bash
npm install @primer/react @primer/primitives react react-dom
```
Primer React no longer needs styled-components.

## Setup
```tsx
import '@primer/primitives/dist/css/functional/themes/light.css';   // import each theme you use
import { BaseStyles, ThemeProvider } from '@primer/react';

export function RootLayout() {
  return <ThemeProvider><BaseStyles><App /></BaseStyles></ThemeProvider>;
}
```
For GitHub.com-style base element styling, also import `@primer/css/dist/primer.css`. Wrap rendered Markdown in `className="markdown-body"`.

## Theme it to a brand
Primer is GitHub's identity; customise through the Primer Primitives CSS variables (`var(--fgColor-default)`, `var(--bgColor-default)`, …) rather than hard-coded colours.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @primer/mcp` for component and token lookup.
- Rails apps: Primer ViewComponents (`primer_view_components` gem). Plain HTML: Primer CSS.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)

  - in-repo package: https://github.com/gluestack/gluestack-ui/tree/HEAD/apps/website (see its README for setup)

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v5, checked against https://gluestack.io/llms-full.txt on 2026-11-05; latest release 5.0.15._

## Install
```bash
npx gluestack-ui init                  # prompts for a styling engine: NativeWind v5 or UniWind (Expo only)
npx gluestack-ui add button input modal
# or every component: npx gluestack-ui add --all
```
`init` writes `gluestack-ui.config.json`, adds `GluestackUIProvider` and the core components (icon, overlay, toast), installs dependencies and updates `metro.config.js`, `babel.config.js`, `global.css` and your entry file. Monorepos: `npx gluestack-ui init --monorepo --path packages/ui`.

## How it works
Copy-paste components (shadcn-style) for React Native and web, styled with Tailwind CSS v4 classes. Works with Expo, React Native CLI and Next.js.

## Setup
Wrap the app in the generated provider: `<GluestackUIProvider mode="light">{children}</GluestackUIProvider>` (`mode` can follow your colour-mode state).

## Theme it to a brand
v5 has no `tailwind.config.js`: theme tokens are shadcn-style semantic variables defined in `global.css`. Edit those for light and dark.

## Agent tips
- Upgrading from v4 or earlier: `npx gluestack-ui@latest upgrade` detects the version and migrates to your chosen engine.
- Full docs for LLMs: `https://gluestack.io/llms-full.txt` (index at `https://gluestack.io/llms.txt`).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v9, checked against https://ionicframework.com/docs/react/quickstart.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 9.0.10._

## Install
```bash
npm install -g @ionic/cli
ionic start myApp tabs --type=react     # or --type=angular / --type=vue
cd myApp && ionic serve
```
Native shells via Capacitor (Ionic 9 supports Capacitor 7+): `npx cap add ios` and `npx cap add android`.

## Theme it to a brand
Set the colour variables (`--ion-color-primary`, its `-rgb`, `-contrast`, `-shade` and `-tint` variants) in your theme CSS file; the colour generator in the docs produces the full set from one hex. Dark mode: import one of `@ionic/<framework>/css/palettes/dark.system.css` (follows the OS), `dark.class.css` (toggle with a class) or `dark.always.css`.

## Agent tips
- Components adapt to iOS and Material styling automatically per platform.
- Keep the `IonPage` / `IonHeader` / `IonContent` structure on every page, or navigation transitions break.
- Upgrading an older app: `npx @ionic/migrate` applies Ionic 9's breaking changes and lists what is left. Angular 18–22 are supported.
- Docs index for LLMs: `https://ionicframework.com/docs/llms.txt`; pages have `.md` versions.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.

4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npx sv create my-app --add tailwindcss     # new SvelteKit app with Tailwind
npx shadcn-svelte@latest init
npx shadcn-svelte@latest add button card dialog
```
Vite, Astro and manual setups have their own guides.

## How it works
Same model as shadcn/ui: source is copied into your project (`$lib/components/ui`), built on Bits UI and Tailwind CSS, and themed with CSS variables. It also supports publishing your own registry.

## Theme it to a brand
Edit the CSS variables in your global stylesheet (`--primary`, `--background`, `--radius`, …) for light and dark.

## Agent tips
- `https://shadcn-svelte.com/llms.txt` indexes every page as Markdown. Use Svelte 5 syntax (runes); older examples use Svelte 4.

## Build checklist (any system)

5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
See https://intentui.com for installation.

## Agent tips
- Read https://intentui.com/llms.txt first. It indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Consider an alternative if
- you are building a commercial or non-government product. Government systems are designed (and sometimes licensed) for public services.

_Hand-written guide for v3, checked against https://designsystem.digital.gov/documentation/getting-started/developers/phase-one-install/ on 2026-11-05; latest release 3.14.0._

## Install
```bash
npm install @uswds/uswds --save-exact
npm install @uswds/compile        # official Sass compile + asset copy tooling (gulp)
npx gulp init                     # copy assets and compile with your gulpfile
```
No build step: the package also ships compiled CSS and JS in `dist/` (`dist/css/uswds.min.css`, `dist/js/uswds.min.js`).

## Theme it to a brand
Set theme settings in `_uswds-theme.scss` with `@use "uswds-core" with (…)`, for example `$theme-color-primary` and `$theme-font-type-sans`. Values are USWDS design tokens such as `"blue-60v"`.

## Agent tips
- Copy markup from each component page and keep the `usa-` classes.
- `https://designsystem.digital.gov/llms.txt` indexes the documentation.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Generated guide (no hand-written guide yet). Prefer the official llms.txt / MCP server for exact setup._

## Install
See https://zardui.com for installation.

## Agent tips
- Read https://zardui.com/llms.txt first. It indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://cloudscape.design/llms.txt
- MCP server: none found

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v3, checked against https://cloudscape.design/get-started/for-developers/using-cloudscape-components/index.html.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 3.0.1410._

## Install
```bash
npm install @cloudscape-design/global-styles @cloudscape-design/components
```

## Setup
```tsx
import '@cloudscape-design/global-styles/index.css';
import Button from '@cloudscape-design/components/button';   // per-component imports
import AppLayout from '@cloudscape-design/components/app-layout';
```
Colour mode and density:
```ts
import { applyMode, applyDensity, Mode, Density } from '@cloudscape-design/global-styles';
applyMode(Mode.Dark);
applyDensity(Density.Compact);
```

## Theme it to a brand
Limited by design: `applyTheme({ theme, selector: 'body' })` from `@cloudscape-design/components/theming` (needs a CSP that allows inline styles), or `generateThemeStylesheet` for build-time CSS.

## Agent tips
- Cloudscape's docs are built for agents: `https://cloudscape.design/llms.txt`, a Markdown version of every page (`…/index.html.md`) and machine-readable component APIs (`https://cloudscape.design/components/index.html.json`, or per component).
- Use the documented patterns (create resource, table view, dashboards), which map one-to-one to components.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

    ```json

    ```

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v1, checked against https://github.com/spartan-ng/spartan/blob/main/skills/spartan/cli.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 1.9.0._

## Install
```bash
npm i -D @spartan-ng/cli
ng g @spartan-ng/cli:init
ng g @spartan-ng/cli:ui-theme          # pick a theme (CSS variables)
ng g @spartan-ng/cli:ui --name=button  # or: ng g @spartan-ng/cli:ui all
```
Nx: use `npx nx g @spartan-ng/cli:…` with the same generators.

## How it works
shadcn/ui's model for Angular: `@spartan-ng/brain` provides accessible headless primitives (installed from npm); `helm` provides Tailwind-styled source copied into your repo, which you own and edit.

## Theme it to a brand
Edit the CSS variables written by `ui-theme` (same model as shadcn/ui: `--primary`, `--background`, `--radius`, …).

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @spartan-ng/mcp`. Agent skill: `npx skills add spartan-ng/spartan`.
- `ng g @spartan-ng/cli:healthcheck --autoFix` checks and repairs the setup.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

Numbers as reported by each source on 2026-11-05; nothing is estimated.

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://webawesome.com/llms.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Agent skills shipped in the npm package:** `webawesome`, `webawesome-design`
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/shoelace-style/webawesome/blob/HEAD/packages/webawesome/docs/docs/tokens/tokens.json
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/shoelace-style/webawesome/blob/HEAD/packages/webawesome/CLAUDE.md


_Hand-written guide for v3, checked against https://webawesome.com/llms.txt on 2026-11-05; latest release 3.14.0._

## Install
No build step needed. In `<head>` (pinned to v3.14.0, the latest release when this page was built):
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://ka-f.webawesome.com/webawesome@3.14.0/styles/themes/default.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://ka-f.webawesome.com/webawesome@3.14.0/styles/utilities.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://ka-f.webawesome.com/webawesome@3.14.0/styles/native.css" />
<script type="module" src="https://ka-f.webawesome.com/webawesome@3.14.0/webawesome.loader.js"></script>
```
Set the theme on `<html>`: `<html class="wa-theme-default wa-palette-default wa-light">` (swap `wa-light` for `wa-dark`, add `wa-brand-<hue>` to re-brand). With a bundler: `npm install @awesome.me/webawesome` and import components individually.

## How it works
Framework-agnostic web components (`<wa-button variant="brand">`) — successor to Shoelace. Works in React, Vue, Svelte, Angular or plain HTML.

## Theme it to a brand
One class re-brands everything: `wa-brand-<hue>` on `<html>`. Finer control: override `--wa-*` tokens in one stylesheet (semantic tokens like `--wa-color-brand-fill-loud`, `--wa-color-surface-raised`, never palette tints). Free themes: default, awesome, shoelace.

## Agent tips
- The package ships two agent skills: `npx skills add ./node_modules/@awesome.me/webawesome/dist/skills/webawesome` (component API) and `.../webawesome-design` (layout, theming, composition). Read them before building.
- Full pages use `<wa-page>` (nav goes in `slot="navigation"` once; it becomes a mobile drawer automatically). Sections use `wa-stack`, `wa-cluster`, `wa-grid`, `wa-split` with `wa-gap-*`.
- No hex, `px` or hand-written flex/grid: use `--wa-*` tokens and layout utilities. Custom elements never self-close.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npm install fundamental-styles
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://sap.github.io/fundamental-styles/

## Agent tips
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `packages/styles/src/theming/common/token/_sap_fiori.scss`). Map brand colours and type onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npm install @hashicorp/design-system-components
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://helios.hashicorp.design

## Agent tips
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `packages/tokens/src`). Map brand colours and type onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.
