  - in-repo package: https://github.com/db-ux-design-system/core-web/tree/HEAD/packages/mcp-server (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/db-ux-design-system/core-web/blob/HEAD/packages/mcp-server/src/tools/tokens.ts
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/db-ux-design-system/core-web/blob/HEAD/.github/copilot-instructions.md
- **Figma Code Connect:** yes, so Figma components map to code.

## Consider an alternative if
- you are not that brand. Deutsche Bahn brand identity.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Generated guide (no hand-written guide yet). Prefer the official llms.txt / MCP server for exact setup._

## Install
```bash
npm install @db-ux/core-components
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://design-system.deutschebahn.com

## Agent tips
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/tokens.ts`). Map brand colours and type onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Web components work in any framework; React 19+ supports them directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.


## Agent tips
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `packages/preset/src/theme/tokens`). Map brand colours and type onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- llms.txt: not published
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@nysds/mcp-server`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"nysds":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@nysds/mcp-server"]}}}
    ```
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/ITS-HCD/nysds/tree/HEAD/packages/mcp-server (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/ITS-HCD/nysds/blob/HEAD/packages/tokens/src
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/ITS-HCD/nysds/blob/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md
- **Figma Code Connect:** yes, so Figma components map to code.

## Consider an alternative if
- you are building a commercial or non-government product. Government systems are designed (and sometimes licensed) for public services.

_Generated guide (no hand-written guide yet). Prefer the official llms.txt / MCP server for exact setup._

## Install
No build step needed. From the CDN (pinned to the current release):
```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@nysds/components@1.23.1/dist/nysds.min.js"></script>
```
Check the docs for the recommended files: https://designsystem.ny.gov
```bash
npm install @nysds/components
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://designsystem.ny.gov

## Agent tips
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `packages/tokens/src`). Map brand colours and type onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Web components work in any framework; React 19+ supports them directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v8, checked against https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit/blob/main/docs/migration-to-v8.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 8.0.0._

## Install
```bash
npm install @gravity-ui/uikit
# optional: @gravity-ui/navigation @gravity-ui/date-components @gravity-ui/icons
```
Requires React 18 or 19. Virtualised and drag-and-drop entry points need extra peers (`@tanstack/react-virtual`, `@hello-pangea/dnd`).

## Setup
```tsx
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css';
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';
import { Provider } from '@gravity-ui/uikit';

<Provider theme="light" lang="en">{/* app */}</Provider>   // themes: light, dark, light-hc, dark-hc
```
v8 replaced the app-level `ThemeProvider` with `Provider` (theme, language, layout, component defaults and mobile settings in one).

## Theme it to a brand
Override the semantic CSS variables (`--g-color-base-brand`, `--g-color-text-brand`, …) per theme; the Themer on gravity-ui.com generates them.

## Agent tips
- v8 moved the old `List`, `Menu`, `DropdownMenu` and `Table` to `@gravity-ui/uikit/legacy`; the root `List` and `Menu` have new APIs. Don't copy v7 examples.
- Layout: the new `Grid` plus responsive props on `Box`, `Flex`, `Container`, `Row` and `Col`.
- `@gravity-ui/navigation` gives a ready app shell (AsideHeader) for consoles.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npm install @primer/view-components
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://primer.style/view-components

## Agent tips
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)

## Consider an alternative if
- you rely on agent tooling. This system has few machine-readable resources.

_Hand-written guide for Compose Material 3, checked against https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3 on 2026-11-05._

## Install
```kotlin
// app/build.gradle.kts
val composeBom = platform("androidx.compose:compose-bom:<latest>")
implementation(composeBom)
implementation("androidx.compose.material3:material3")
```
The BOM keeps all Compose library versions aligned; check the Compose BOM page for the latest version.

## Setup
```kotlin
MaterialTheme(
  colorScheme = when {
    dynamicColor && darkTheme -> dynamicDarkColorScheme(LocalContext.current)
    dynamicColor && !darkTheme -> dynamicLightColorScheme(LocalContext.current)
    darkTheme -> DarkColorScheme
    else -> LightColorScheme
  },
  typography = AppTypography,
) { App() }
```
Dynamic colour is available on Android 12+.

## Theme it to a brand
Generate `LightColorScheme`, `DarkColorScheme` and typography from brand colours with Material Theme Builder, which exports Compose theme code (`Color.kt`, `Theme.kt`, `Type.kt`).

## Agent tips
- Use `Scaffold`, `TopAppBar` and the navigation components (`NavigationBar`, `NavigationSuiteScaffold`) for adaptive layouts.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Generated guide (no hand-written guide yet). Prefer the official llms.txt / MCP server for exact setup._

## Install
```bash
npm install @digdir/designsystemet-react
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://designsystemet.no

## Agent tips
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `design-tokens/$themes.json`). Map brand colours and type onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Web components work in any framework; React 19+ supports them directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

| Capability | Points |
|---|---|
| Official MCP server (agent can query components/docs live) | 0/20 |
| llms.txt on the docs site | 0/15 |

- llms.txt: not published
- MCP server: none found

## Consider an alternative if
- you are not building inside the apple ecosystem.
- you rely on agent tooling. This system has few machine-readable resources.

_Hand-written guide for SwiftUI (iOS 26 SDK), checked against https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui on 2026-11-05._

## Install
Built into Xcode and SwiftUI; no dependency.

## Setup
Use system components and styles so the Human Interface Guidelines are followed automatically: `NavigationStack` / `NavigationSplitView`, `TabView`, `List`, `Form`, `.toolbar`, `.searchable`, `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)`, semantic colours (`Color.primary`, `Color(.systemBackground)`), Dynamic Type text styles (`.font(.headline)`) and SF Symbols.

## Theme it to a brand
Set `.tint(Color("Brand"))` at the root and define colours in the asset catalog with light and dark variants. Avoid fixed font sizes and custom navigation chrome.

## Agent tips
- Check the HIG page for a component before inventing a pattern.
- Test Dynamic Type, Dark Mode and VoiceOver in previews (`#Preview` with `.environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, .accessibility3)`).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Consider an alternative if
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v22, checked against https://github.com/angular/components/blob/main/guides/getting-started.md on 2026-11-05; latest release 22.2.6._

## Install
```bash
ng add @angular/material
```

## Setup
Import components directly into standalone components:
```ts
import { MatButtonModule } from '@angular/material/button';
import { MatSlideToggle } from '@angular/material/slide-toggle';

@Component({ imports: [MatButtonModule, MatSlideToggle], template: `<mat-slide-toggle>Toggle me</mat-slide-toggle>` })
export class App {}
```

## Theme it to a brand
```scss
@use '@angular/material' as mat;

html {
  color-scheme: light dark;   // follows the OS; use `light` or `dark` to force one
  @include mat.theme((
    color: (primary: mat.$violet-palette, tertiary: mat.$orange-palette),
    typography: Inter,
    density: 0,
  ));
}
body { background: var(--mat-sys-surface); color: var(--mat-sys-on-surface); }
```
Fine-tune with `mat.<component>-overrides((...))` mixins and the `--mat-sys-*` CSS variables.

## Agent tips
- Angular's own LLM docs: `https://angular.dev/llms.txt`. The Angular Material site does not publish an llms.txt.
- Use the CDK (`@angular/cdk`) for overlays, drag and drop and virtual scrolling before reaching for third-party libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```bash
npm install flowbite
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://flowbite.com

## Agent tips
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code, and use it to look up components and props.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npm install @material/web
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://material-web.dev

## Agent tips
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `testing/tokens.ts`). Map brand colours and type onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Web components work in any framework; React 19+ supports them directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- MCP server: none found
- **Copy-the-source CLI:** documented at https://ai-sdk.dev/elements/llms.txt
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements/blob/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.

_Hand-written guide for v1, checked against https://ai-sdk.dev/elements/llms.txt on 2026-11-05; latest release 1.9.1._

## Install
Prerequisites: React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui (set up automatically if missing) and the AI SDK (`npm i ai @ai-sdk/react zod`).
```bash
npx ai-elements@latest                      # pick components interactively
npx ai-elements@latest add message
# or via the shadcn CLI: npx shadcn@latest add @ai-elements/message
```

## What you get
Composable chat and agent UI as source in your repo: `Message` / `MessageContent` / `MessageResponse` (streaming Markdown), prompt input, reasoning, tool calls, sources, code blocks and more, aware of AI SDK streaming states.

## Agent tips
- Pair with `useChat` from `@ai-sdk/react`; components take AI SDK message types (`UIMessage`).
- Choose it alongside a base system (usually shadcn/ui), not instead of one.
- Unstyled components usually mean the shadcn/ui Tailwind 4 setup (globals.css) is missing.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Build checklist (any system)

2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bulma@1.0.4/css/bulma.min.css">
```
Check the docs for the recommended files: https://bulma.io
```bash
npm install bulma
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://bulma.io

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use. Check the docs for RSC support.
- you rely on agent tooling. This system has few machine-readable resources.

_Generated guide (no hand-written guide yet). Prefer the official llms.txt / MCP server for exact setup._

## Install
```bash
npm install @strapi/design-system
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://design-system.strapi.io

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.


## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```bash
npm install @zendeskgarden/react-buttons
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://garden.zendesk.com

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```bash
npm install @trendyol/baklava
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://baklava.design

## Agent tips
- Web components work in any framework; React 19+ supports them directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- MCP server: none found

## Consider an alternative if
- you are building a commercial or non-government product. Government systems are designed (and sometimes licensed) for public services.
- you need a no-build page (plain HTML from a CDN). This needs a bundler.
- you rely on agent tooling. This system has few machine-readable resources.

_Hand-written guide for v6, checked against https://frontend.design-system.service.gov.uk/import-css/ on 2026-11-05; latest release 6.6.0._

## Install
```bash
npm install govuk-frontend
```
For quick prototypes, the GOV.UK Prototype Kit is the supported route: `npx govuk-prototype-kit create my-prototype`.

## Setup
CSS, either precompiled or from Sass (needs Dart Sass 1.79+):
```scss
@use "node_modules/govuk-frontend/dist/govuk" as *;
```
or `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/govuk-frontend.min.css">` after copying it from `node_modules/govuk-frontend/dist/govuk/`.

JavaScript, before `</body>`:
```html
<script type="module" src="/assets/govuk-frontend.min.js"></script>
<script type="module">
  import { initAll } from '/assets/govuk-frontend.min.js'
  initAll()
</script>
```
Markup: use the Nunjucks macros (`{{ govukButton({ text: "Continue" }) }}`) or copy the HTML from each component page.

## Agent tips
- v6 uses the GOV.UK brand colours and the new type scale; `govuk-body-xs` and `govuk-!-font-size-14` are gone.
- Follow the **patterns** (question pages, check answers, confirmation): they encode tested UX for transactional services.
- GOV.UK services can't change the brand. For a non-GOV.UK product use your own country's government system, or USWDS, which is more themeable.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.


## Setup
```tsx
import '@salt-ds/theme/index.css';
import { SaltProvider, Button } from '@salt-ds/core';
<SaltProvider mode="light" density="medium">{/* density: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' | 'touch' */}</SaltProvider>
```

## Agent tips
- Use `density="high"` for trading and data-dense screens; an AG Grid theme is published as `@salt-ds/ag-grid-theme`.
- Salt's identity is J.P. Morgan's by default; theme it before using it for another brand.
- No released MCP server yet: `@salt-ds/mcp` exists on npm only as a snapshot build.

_Generated guide (no hand-written guide yet). Prefer the official llms.txt / MCP server for exact setup._

## Install
```bash
npm install vue-element-plus-x
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://element-plus-x.com

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
No build step needed. From the CDN (pinned to the current release):
```html
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@astrouxds/astro-web-components@8.0.1/dist/astro-web-components/astro-web-components.esm.min.js"></script>
```
Check the docs for the recommended files: https://www.astrouxds.com
```bash
npm install @astrouxds/astro-web-components
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://www.astrouxds.com

## Agent tips
- Web components work in any framework; React 19+ supports them directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

_Generated guide (no hand-written guide yet). Prefer the official llms.txt / MCP server for exact setup._

## Install
```bash
npm install @gouvfr/dsfr
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://www.systeme-de-design.gouv.fr

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Build checklist (any system)

2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```bash
npm install @melt-ui/svelte
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://melt-ui.com

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider:** follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens:** set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first:** build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components:** map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States:** loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility:** keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness:** enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify:** run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.
